ai.description: *Micrixalus uttaraghati* is a small frog (22–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored venter. It is distinguished by a prominent white throat and the male's characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus uttaraghati* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright white or pale yellow patch on the throat, which is absent in other *Micrixalus* species.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus uttaraghati* inhabits the rocky, fast-flowing streams of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, male *Micrixalus uttaraghati* perform "foot-flagging," extending and waving their hind legs to attract mates and signal rivals near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus uttaraghati* is an egg-laying frog that breeds during the monsoon season, depositing small clutches of eggs in hidden crevices beneath stream-bed rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus uttaraghati* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in the Indian states of Maharashtra and Gujarat, typically found at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Northern Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rapid series of short, metallic chirps, typically heard near fast-flowing, rocky streams in the Western Ghats.
